meta.title: UzOS — a learning operating system
meta.description: UzOS is a small 32-bit x86 operating system written to be read. Download the ISO, boot it in QEMU or VirtualBox, and see how memory, processes and security really work.

hero.title: An operating system
hero.subtitle: UzOS is a small x86 operating system with clean, commented code. Boot it in a virtual machine in one minute, then open the source and see how processes, memory, users and security really work.
hero.note: Free and open source · {size} MB ISO · runs in QEMU and VirtualBox

modules.title: The 12 managements of an operating system
modules.subtitle: Every big part of an OS has its own module. Ten are ready to explore today, two are next.

structure.title: One folder, one idea
structure.subtitle: Every management is built the same way. Learn the layout once and you can find your way in all of them.

core.title: core/
core.text: Only the parts the kernel itself calls, like the timer tick or the scheduler.

commands.title: commands/
commands.text: One folder for each shell command, with its own .c and .h file.

syscalls.title: syscalls/
syscalls.text: One folder for each system call a program can make.

security.title: security/
security.text: One folder for each attack, with the defence that stops it inside.

structure.principlesTitle: Why it is easy to learn

principles.title: Self-contained
principles.text: Everything a command needs is inside its folder. Open one folder, understand one thing.

principles.title: Explained in place
principles.text: Every file starts with a comment: what it does, what it uses, and why it is built this way.

principles.title: Nothing hidden
principles.text: Every #include uses the full path and says what it takes, so you always see which file is used.

principles.title: Break it, then fix it
principles.text: Each attack sits next to its defence. Run it, watch it get blocked, then read how.

structure.codeCaption: A real file from UzOS: one system call, one folder.

quickstart.title: Running in three steps
quickstart.subtitle: Nothing is installed on your disk. UzOS boots inside a virtual machine.

step1.title: Download the ISO
step1.text: One {size} MB file. It is the whole operating system.

step2.title: Install QEMU
step2.text: A free emulator for Linux, Windows and macOS.

step3.title: Boot it
step3.text: Log in as root (password uzos) and type help.

screenshots.title: See it running
screenshots.subtitle: Real screenshots, taken from UzOS running in QEMU.

uzfetch.label: System
uzfetch.caption: uzfetch shows the system next to the flag; ps lists the processes.

seclab.label: Security lab
seclab.caption: A fork bomb runs live, and its defence slot_quota blocks it.

htop.label: Processes
htop.caption: htop while the fork bomb's 8 processes share the CPU.

btop.label: Monitor
btop.caption: btop: CPU history, memory and processes in boxes.

audit.label: Audit
audit.caption: audit shows what was refused and to whom; caps shows the privileges of guest.

memory.label: Memory
memory.caption: meminfo shows physical RAM; pagewalk follows an address through the page tables.

files.label: Files
files.caption: Files with owners and permissions, and a /proc file written by the kernel.

help.label: Commands
help.caption: help lists all 83 commands in groups.

desktop.label: Desktop
desktop.caption: startx opens a small desktop with windows you can drag.

boot.label: Boot
boot.caption: The boot log: one line for every part of the kernel that starts.

learn.title: Made for students and the curious
learn.text: UzOS is a teaching project. The code is short, commented, and split so that each folder answers one question: how does paging work? How does the scheduler choose? What stops a fork bomb?

footer.tagline: A small operating system for learning how computers really work.

management.sourceNote: The descriptions below come straight from the comments in the UzOS source code, so they are always up to date and written in English.

core.title: Core parts
core.intro: The parts the kernel itself calls. Each one is a folder with its own .c and .h file.

commands.title: Commands
commands.intro: Type these in the UzOS shell. Each command lives in its own folder, commands/<name>/, with cmd_<name>.c and cmd_<name>.h.

syscalls.title: System calls
syscalls.intro: How a program asks the kernel for help: it puts the number in EAX and runs int 0x80. Each call lives in syscalls/<name>/ with sys_<name>.c and sys_<name>.h.

security.title: Attacks and defences
security.intro: Every attack breaks one rule of the kernel, and the defence next to it stops it. Run seclab attack <id> to simulate safely, add live to really run it, and seclab repair to clean up.

invariants.resource: resources: slots, PIDs, stacks and memory are limited
invariants.identity: identity: a PID always names exactly one process
invariants.isolation: isolation: processes cannot touch each other's memory
invariants.privilege: privilege: user code cannot act with kernel rights
invariants.liveness: liveness: no process can starve the others
invariants.disclosure: disclosure: no leaking of old or foreign data
invariants.trust: trust: input from outside is checked before use
invariants.integrity: integrity: kernel code and the audit log stay unchanged
